prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Business software subscription pricing (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Plan" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Price" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Minimum seats" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Contract" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Support" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Plan" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Price › List price" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 67px
  col 3: header "Price › Billing terms" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 490px
  col 4: header "Minimum seats" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 109px
  col 5: header "Contract" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "Support" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 195px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A procurement/comparison reference: pick a plan (row) and read its price, how it is billed, seat minimums, contract and support terms. It is scanned vertically by plan and compared horizontally by attribute.","reading":"Reader anchors on column 1 (Plan), reads the bold price, then the billing-terms sentence that explains it, then the three short constraint/attribute columns (seats, contract, support) as a quick checklist. So the eye moves plan → price pair → terms strip, and column 3's long prose is the one cell that must wrap.","groups":["cols 2+3 (Price group): 'List price' is the number, 'Billing terms' its explanation — they must stay adjacent under the merged 'Price' header and be read as a pair","cols 4,5,6 (Minimum seats / Contract / Support): same role — short attribute values in a checklist strip; they should share a similar, compact rhythm even if their headers are narrower than one line","col 1 (Plan) stands alone as row identity and needs a clean, uninterrupted edge"],"keep_intact":["Plan names (Education = 75px) — never split a row identifier","Currency amounts ($12, $45) and the price column header 'List price' (67px)","Numeric seat values in 'Minimum seats'","Short contract/support values and their header words if any scroll budget exists"],"may_wrap":["Billing terms prose (490px one-line) — the natural flexible column; 2–6 lines are acceptable and absorb row-height growth","'Minimum seats', 'Contract', 'Support' headers into two lines if width forces it","Billing-terms header word 'Billing' only as a last resort"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [96, 88, 220, 100, 105, 125] · table 735×547px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 375px
Design r2B: widths [96, 88, 150, 95, 95, 110] · table 635×756px · row heights [36, 36, 83, 106, 129, 129, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 275px
Design r2C: widths [96, 88, 170, 109, 123, 150] · table 737×686px · row heights [36, 36, 83, 83, 106, 106, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 377px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
